known_facts_book1: The wife of Uncle Henry, a Kansas farmer's wife, and the aunt who is raising the orphan Dorothy.
Was once a young, pretty wife, but the sun and wind turned her thin and gray and sober, and she never laughs.
Screams and runs for the cellar when the cyclone comes, unable to reach Dorothy in time.
Is the home Dorothy longs to return to throughout the book, and runs out to catch Dorothy in her arms at the very end.
Does not travel to Oz and never appears in the Land of Oz.

known_relations_book1.Dorothy: Her orphaned niece and ward, whom she loves though gray life has left her grave.

known_facts_book1: A Kansas farmer, Dorothy's uncle and Aunt Em's husband, gray from his long beard to his rough boots, who works hard and never laughs.
Watches the sky, warns of the coming cyclone, and runs to look after the cattle and the horses before taking shelter.
Does not travel to Oz; when Dorothy returns he is milking the cows in the barnyard.
Never appears in the Land of Oz.
hallucination_signals: Uncle Henry is carried by the cyclone to Oz

known_facts_book1: A rich Munchkin, one of the leading men of the eastern country, who hosts Dorothy for her first night in Oz.
Recognises Dorothy as a great sorceress because she wears the Silver Shoes and white dress and has killed the Wicked Witch of the East.
Tells her that white is the witches' colour and blue the Munchkins' colour, so her checked blue-and-white dress marks her as a friend.
Gives her supper, a bed, and a good breakfast before she goes on toward the Emerald City.
Appears only in the Munchkin country near the start of the journey.

known_relations_book1.Dorothy: The Munchkin who houses and feeds her on her first night in Oz.
known_relations_book1.Munchkins: One of their leading and wealthy men.

known_facts_book1: The little Queen of the thousands of gray field mice, saved by the Tin Woodman when he kills a wildcat that is chasing her.
In gratitude she and her mice tie themselves to a truck the Tin Woodman builds and haul the sleeping Cowardly Lion out of the deadly poppy field.
Gives Dorothy a little whistle to summon her, telling her to blow it whenever she needs the mice.
Comes when Dorothy later whistles and advises her to use the Golden Cap to call the Winged Monkeys.
Is fearful of the Lion at first, sure he would eat all the mice, until told he is a coward and a friend.

known_relations_book1.Tin Woodman: Her rescuer, who kills the wildcat pursuing her.
known_relations_book1.Cowardly Lion: Whom her mice drag from the poppy field despite their fear of him.
known_relations_book1.Dorothy: Whom she gives a summoning whistle and later guides toward the Emerald City.

known_facts_book1: The King of the Winged Monkeys, who obeys whoever wears the Golden Cap and its charm.

Tells Dorothy the legend of the Cap: how a monkey band once dropped the dandy Quelala into a river for sport and were bound to serve the Golden Cap's owner three times as punishment by the princess Gayelette.
Explains that no owner may command the Monkeys more than three times.
Carries the travellers where they are bidden, once for the Wicked Witch of the West and later for Dorothy and for Glinda.
Refuses only one request: he cannot carry Dorothy across the desert out of the Land of Oz, saying the Monkeys belong only to this country and may never leave it.

known_relations_book1.Dorothy: Whom he carries by force of the Golden Cap's charm, first as the Witch's captive and later at Dorothy's own command.
known_relations_book1.Wicked Witch: Of the West, who commanded his band with the Golden Cap to seize the travellers.
known_relations_book1.Glinda: To whom the Golden Cap passes, and whom the Monkeys then obey.
known_relations_book1.Gayelette: The princess who long ago bound his grandfather's band to the Cap.
known_relations_book1.Quelala: The man his grandfather's band once dropped in the river.

known_facts_book1: The green-clad, greenish-skinned man who keeps the gate of the Emerald City, clothed all in green with a green box at his side.
Locks a pair of green spectacles onto each visitor before they may enter, keeping the only key on a chain around his neck, because Oz ordered everyone to wear them.
Leads the travellers through the streets to the Palace when they first arrive.
Later unlocks their spectacles when they leave, and tells them there is no road across the deadly desert that rings the Land of Oz.
Is amazed and glad to hear that Dorothy has melted the Wicked Witch of the West.

known_relations_book1.Dorothy: Whom he admits to the Emerald City and fits with spectacles.
known_relations_book1.Wizard: Whose order to wear locked spectacles he enforces at the gate.

known_facts_book1: A little china clown in the Dainty China Country, one of its people, dressed in red and yellow and green.
Is always trying to stand upon his head and has broken and been mended so often that he is covered with cracks.
Greets Dorothy with a saucy rhyme mocking how stiff and prim she looks, then stands on his head.
The china Princess tells Dorothy he is cracked in the head and foolish, and to pay him no mind.
Appears only briefly during Dorothy's passage through the China Country.

known_relations_book1.Dorothy: A china figure who teases her when she passes through the China Country.
